title: The Place That Time Forgot
subtitle: Excellent, everything is going according to plan. "Fate" will not reveal its hand—at least, for now.

trails.title: National Foucault Studies Association
trails.description: They brandish philosophy to persecute all "heretics" equally.

content.text: All it takes is one lie to set off a chain reaction, and I'm afraid the butterfly effect has reached you. I have bad news. You've been betrayed.
But there's good news, too: a certain flight lieutenant appears to be more loyal to you than to the organization she swore to serve.

branch.text: You know him—the admiral who was pitted against an enemy he couldn't possibly defeat. This conflict has left an incurable ulcer in his once lofty heart.
Yet, as a leader, he must remain unyielding in both body and mind.
Despite his continued victories on the front lines, he made a decision so counterintuitive that even his loyal adjutant found it questionable.
The top brass always sees things differently, I suppose.

content.text: Things never end well for traitors.

branch.text: You must have heard the story of the Trojan Horse, right?

Greek soldiers sneaked past the walls of Troy inside a wooden horse. One Trojan priest tried to warn his people, but was executed by the gods themselves for doing so. Soon after, all the leaders of Troy were killed by the hidden invaders.
Being killed by your enemy is bad; being killed by your ally is worse. It was an honorless way to go.
Don't get your hopes up. He's more like a desperate patient than anything. Weary from the pain of his ulcer, and frantically searching for a way out.
In his desperation, he has clutched at an opportunity presented by none other than the Preacher herself.
Deep down, he knows he's backed himself into a corner.
Great. I'm done reading reports anyway.
I look forward to your wise decisions. We need some good news for a change.

content.text: Hopefully, he knows what he's doing.

items.text: The Place That Time Forgot
Comala Prison Perimeter
The gray riverbed winds through the frostbitten earth, disappearing into the distant horizon.
A neat yet dilapidated circular complex stands alone beneath the snow-capped mountains, as if abandoned by God, humanity, and ghosts alike.
Outside the fence, three uninvited guests discuss their plan to get inside.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Behold! Comala Prison! It's the biggest building around. When the sun comes out, it looks like a rusty button stitched into the earth.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Everyone tries not to pay attention to it, but it's undoubtedly one of the most important places in town. This way, careful, we're heading uphill—Oops!
The young writer begins to slip again. She is prevented only by Sonetto's quick reflexes.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Phew! Thanks. So, my new friends! You're from that St. Palomino's ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And Vertin is the Timekeeper there.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Ah, very impressive! Sounds all official and polished! Then, I take it you've already got a way into the prison?
The gate presents an unwelcoming face to the world.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'll draft a letter to headquarters right away. Once they approve it, they'll notify the local branch in Buenos Aires. From there, they'll need to inform the Argentine government,

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: who will then issue us a permit.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Excellent! Looks like our bureaucrats still have some worth. No offense intended, of course.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Since we're pressed for time, I believe we can ask that headquarters give high priority to our request. If all goes well, we should have the permit in about a month.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Ah. How, how expedient of them! But you know what? Maybe we shouldn't bother all those hard-working government officials with these trifling matters after all.
She instantly returns to her previous judgment.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I have a simpler solution that suits the urgency of our cause!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That sounds great. Oh! Umm, where are you going, Ms. Recoleta?
Before anyone can stop her, the young writer hurls herself up the wall, scaling the side with the sort of skill that immediately suggests she's done this before.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: To the other side of the wall, of course! From Guadalajara to Ushuaia, there has yet to be a wall that could stop me!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Come on, ladies of the Foundation! Sonetto, take my hand!
Sonetto looks utterly flustered.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Recoleta, please! A reckless act like that could have serious consequences! Please come back down!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: In fact, while the details of our mission are classified, I should warn you, it may be dangerous, and we cannot guarantee your safety once we're inside. Perhaps it's in your best interest to return to town.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What? That is definitely not in my best interest!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What sort of pusillanimous coward would I be if I just abandoned my fated companions here? Of course, I'm going in with you, or rather, you're coming with me!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please get down, Ms. Recoleta. Someone's coming our way.
From the other side of the prison fence, a predator's gaze locks onto the figure perched on the wall.
Stop right there! What do you think you're doing?!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Damn! It's her again. The jailer of Comala!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Did she say jailer or jaguar?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Ms. Recoleta. Haven't I made myself clear? I don't want to see you here again.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Jailer! We meet again! What a delightful encounter on such a—
A sudden gust of cold wind interrupts her.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: —lovely day!

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Would you please just leave this place alone?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I'll never understand why a promising young woman like you keeps snooping around a prison.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: I can't make this any clearer: trying to break into Comala will do nothing to get you inside, but it will get you into a world of trouble with the gendarmes.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: So, will you stop these senseless break-in attempts?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Comala Prison is only accessible to academic researchers and journalists, and even they must have official credentials in order to enter.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Isn't there any other way to pay a visit? I truly do need to get in there.
She racks her brain for a plausible excuse.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry to interrupt, but did you just say "official credentials"?

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Yes, you heard me right. And you are?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm the Timekeeper of the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: My assistant and I are here to visit Comala Prison on official orders from the Foundation. Here, this is my ID.
At the thought of lying, Sonetto's lips fail to open for even a squeak. She goes flush red with embarrassment.
Through the prison fence, the jailer examines the pair as she takes the ID in her sizeable paws.
It is at least a very presentable-looking card, boldly stamped with the seal of the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: This is indeed legitimate.
She murmurs.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Welcome to Comala Prison.

items.speaker: Jailer
items.text: Apologies for my earlier behavior. It's been a while since we've had any official visitors.
